originality.rationale: The 2009 article proves only the uniform bound omega(n)>=k-1, giving three for k=4 (Proposition 11), and its 18-prime theorem assumes n odd, which contradicts n=4 beta(n). The 2013/2014 survey states local beta formulas but no seven-prime obstruction; exact 2-adic parity plus a strict rational support bound gives an additional all-size result. Targeted mathematical research-record searches for beta(n)=n/4 and omega>=7 found no equal/stronger claim. Residual priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent unindexed or pre-digital theorem may exist; literature review cannot prove global publication priority. The result is a necessary condition, not existence or sharpness.

value.rationale: The existence of 4-imperfect numbers is an explicitly posed number-theoretic question. This universal restriction raises the known published general support floor for multiplier four from at least 3 to at least 7 without assumptions on exponent or size, by a nontrivial 2-adic parity constraint and a strict rational product threshold. It is a necessary-condition advance, not merely a finite census.
